subject: R and ggplot2 dashboards online and within Shiny using D3.js

messages.author: 67abb4e3d385ca02
messages.subject: R and ggplot2 dashboards online and within Shiny using D3.js
parts:
Hi all,

I recently browsed through the ggplot2 list and saw a few messages from Susan VanderPlas, Ramnath, Mike Dylan and a few others about interactive ggplot2. I thought I'd let folks know about two ways of integrating ggplot2 with D3.js. We'd love your advice and feedback.

First, to make ggplot2 graphs interactive, you can add one line of code to you ggplot2 script. Your plots get a URL, for example: https://plot.ly/~chris/2223/price-vs-carat/. The plot is drawn with D3.js and is interactive. You can embed, zoom, toggle, and see text on the hover from any browser or device. 

Install plotly to get started, then make plots public or private. These docs--a Carson Sievert project--track coverage for the figure converter. 

Shiny also allows you connect to the ggplot2 figure converter, make an interactive graph in a Shiny app, then save the graph and share as a URL or add collaborators. Here is a tutorial. Your published apps let you zoom, toggle, filter, pan, and see data on the hover.

For a dashboard overview, see: http://blog.plot.ly/post/123617968702/online-dashboards-eight-helpful-tips-you-should.

Feedback and suggestions are welcome and appreciated!

M

What have you tried doing? 

I realize you might be frustrated with this answer, but please have a look at the FAQ and make sure you've got what you need. 

If you're installing binaries, you should be ok, but it looks like you're not installing dependencies or those that are, aren't installing correctly. 

Best thing to do is to look at what the errors are and reinstall those packages until it does work. So you needed jsonlite and DBI. Install those and see what else breaks. It's slow, but eventually gets the job done. 

B
